summary.headline: Craftsman guides standalone capex above INR 1,000 crore and consolidated about INR 1,500 crore for FY27, with heavy-HP stationary engine revenue targeted at USD 100 million by FY29-30.
summary.overview:
Management described Q1 FY27 as showing reasonable growth, with aluminium the fastest-growing segment and Industrial margins lifted by stronger material handling and storage demand. Sunbeam restructuring is mostly complete, with about 90% targeted by December and an exit-rate EBITDA margin of mid-teens in Q4. The call centred on capex: standalone spend averaging over INR 1,000 crore a year, INR 430 crore approved for DR Axion, and a new Hosur high-pressure die casting unit. Powertrain capacity utilisation averages around 70%, roughly 10% below optimum by management's account. The company said capex will be funded from internal accruals, and the land deal for expansion is close to signing.</overview>

segments.name: Powertrain
segments.commentary: Utilisation averages around 70%, with festive-season peaks near 75-80% for short periods; management says annualised 80% is unrealistic and it operates about 10% below optimum capacity. Heavy-HP stationary engine opportunity sits here, with 6 large customers in the pipeline.

segments.name: Aluminium (alloy wheels and castings)
segments.commentary: Operating above 80% utilisation. Alloy wheel installed capacity 5.8 million wheels, with expected output of over 4 million this year at Bhiwadi and Shoolagiri; expansion only when utilisation crosses 80%. 4-wheeler revenue is the larger share, followed by 2-wheeler.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Margins rose on higher demand in material handling and storage; management says orders are rising quarter on quarter and the uptick is not a one-off spike. Contract manufacturing described as steady.

segments.name: Sunbeam
segments.commentary: Restructuring nearly complete; exits of legacy, loss-making products are delayed by customer handholding. Management expects top line down 10-20% but gross margin up, with Q4 exit EBITDA margin in the mid-teens.

segments.name: DR Axion (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Substantial capex with INR 430 crore approved; land bought last year; production start pencilled in for FY29 and FY30 on orders in hand.

guidance_outlook: Heavy-HP stationary engine (Kothavadi casting plus Arasur machining) revenue target of USD 100 million in FY29, reiterated as on track; management says FY30 is the first full-revenue year.
Of the first-set products, about 30% productionised by FY28 and a further 50% in FY29; new order wins expected to reach production by FY30-31.
Sunbeam Q4 FY27 exit EBITDA margin mid-teens; restructuring about 90% complete by December.

FY27 consolidated capex about INR 1,500 crore (standalone ~INR 1,000 crore + DR Axion INR 430 crore + maintenance at Sunbeam), described as conservative; Board to revisit capex in Q3 or Q4 if traction holds.
Capex to be funded from internal accruals; no plan to raise from public markets; management says net debt to EBITDA is on track.
Powertrain EBIT margins expected to hold similar return ratios within a couple of years; start-up costs for new stationary-engine capacity to depress margins temporarily.
capex_capacity: Hosur Unit 3: new high-pressure die casting capacity, mainly for automotive parts (2-wheeler and 4-wheeler possible); built in phases over 4-6 quarters or up to 2 years; not for alloy wheels.
Alloy wheel capacity: installed 5.8 million wheels; no new capacity until utilisation exceeds 80%, then marginal expansion.
Greenfield plant basic infrastructure (land, building, ETP/HTP, power, roads) estimated at INR 150-250 crore before production equipment; DR Axion land of about 50 acres cost about INR 150 crore.
Replacing 2016-equivalent capacity now estimated at 5-7x cost; land up 8-9x, construction up 3-4x, machinery roughly doubled in rupee terms.
Land deal for a new site: close to signing per management.
demand_pricing: Heavy-HP stationary engines: 6 large customers; orders received from 5, 1 more expected shortly; first 4 customers' orders cover the USD 100 million FY29-30 target.
Pilot machining running at 2 customers for production; casting validation needs about another year.
Aluminium: new orders coming in; some quick wins to revenue within a couple of quarters, others in development for FY28-FY29 production.
Material cost pass-through: management says pass-through on alloy prices is accepted in principle but varies by customer, with some customers slow to adjust.
Industrial: demand upswing attributed to the India capex cycle in material handling and storage; contract manufacturing steady.

qa_highlights.question: Which powertrain segments and products are growing, and what is the aluminium outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said aluminium will keep growing faster than other segments due to recent investment and capacity still maturing; 4-wheeler is the larger revenue share, with 2-wheeler close behind.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Kothavadi stationary engine order book and Sunbeam profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: USD 100 million FY29 target reiterated; Kothavadi is casting only and billing sits with Arasur. Sunbeam restructuring mostly done, with about 90% complete by December and mid-teens exit EBITDA in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan split between standalone and subsidiaries, and is INR 1,500 crore the right number?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone averages over INR 1,000 crore; DR Axion INR 430 crore approved, with pacing dependent on orders; INR 1,500 crore called conservative, with a possible upward revision at Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How long from low-volume approval to full production for heavy-HP engines, and what margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Casting validation about a year for the first two products; 30% productionised by FY28 and 50% in FY29. New programmes expected in two years. Management expects return ratios similar to the current powertrain within a couple of years, with temporary margin dilution from start-up costs.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Industrial segment's step-up this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher demand in material handling and lifting and storage products from the India capex cycle, with orders rising quarter on quarter and operating leverage lifting margins.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Powertrain averages about 70%, peaking near 75-80% in festive season; aluminium above 80%.
